scope: One scratch-only historical WaveOut storage control, plus baseline, compiled as the complete canonical DirectSound unit and linked with all14 frozen native application objects. DLLs were not executed. No source declarations or target assignments were promoted.

hypothesis.basis: The independent Nemu0.7 and0.7a images prove an actual4-byte HWAVEOUT slot and32-byte WAVEHDR object through native WaveOut APIs. Their retention in the2003 DirectSound unit is not established, and the semantic private names are inferred.

regression_method: Every complete .text section byte string and actual relocation offset/type/target is compared with the frozen objects for DirectSound and AudioLog. Externally named targets preserve names; compiler-generated local labels are identified by the actual unchanged section/value. Symbol-table indices and generated-label counters change when declarations are added. Both raw sets of relocation records are retained; no original instruction bytes are normalized.
body_status_limit: The original-target diagnostics still distinguish non-relocation equality, unresolved and inferred target identities, and actual target mismatches. The three previously unmatched host functions remain unmatched. Identical baseline/candidate COFF records prove absence of new code changes, not whole-DLL success.
displacement_limit: Closer absolute addresses do not establish correct common order or source ownership. This records individual improvements/worsenings only; names and historical2003 retention remain unproved.
findings: All60 complete host code spans retain identical raw bytes and actual relocation targets. The22 differing compiler-generated local-label names refer to exactly the same section/value; their complete old/new records are retained.

Original-target diagnostics remain46/49 DirectSound plus11/11 AudioLog instruction matches. The same2 unresolved targets and63 target mismatches remain; unresolved/inferred identities are not relabeled as complete byte-exact functions.

The two real typed declarations add36 object bytes but64 bytes of whole .data virtual extent, from1279532 to1279596. The whole original-data deficit decreases416 to352 bytes. This can only be a capacity compatibility result.
WaveOutHandle is allocated at0x1016b408. AudioInstance and ABIFile move4 bytes; the following SoundEvents array remains at0x1016b420, absorbing this handle into existing alignment.

WaveOutHeader is allocated at0x1016b920. IsNTSC and CPURegisters move48 bytes, and AudioIniFile and following common objects move64 bytes after normal alignment. No manual alignment, fillers or name variants were used.
Every Mp3 and AudioLog common address remains unchanged. The independently tracked res-to-LogInstance distance stays2308 bytes; this control does not disturb that relation.

These objects are independently proved in both WaveOut historical releases, but neither retention in2003 nor the private names used here is established. No original address is assigned to either new symbol, and no canonical declaration is promoted.
decision: Do not promote based on capacity coincidence. Original2003 retention, private identifiers and exact known common placement remain required evidence.
